newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude - Weak demand forces Tapis out of Asia.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude - Weak demand forces Tapis out of Asia.

text.p: Asian crude oil prices weakened forcing prompt supplies out of the region after finding limited demand in Asia, traders said on Thursday.
A western trader was widely heard taking a million barrels of July Tapis crude to the West, after purchasing the barrels at low levels from a producer.

But traders did not expect Asia's light crude market to be tight because of this. The movement of barrels out of the region, coupled with smaller production from Australia should however improve the recent discounts for the light grades, they said.
August trading for Asian crudes has started, with the first August Bach Ho sold to a major for Australia, at OSP +57/58 cents per barrel.
Although the level was thought strong as Bach Ho's OSP is already firm at Minas APPI +80, traders considered the price in line with the current strength in the heavy Asian crude market.
But the Middle East crude market remains bearish.
The latest trades for Oman were done at MPM -38, and MPM -39 cents per barrel.
A western trader sold Oman at MPM -38 to a shosha, while a US major heard bought a cargo at MPM -39.
An August Masila cargo was also heard sold to Thailand at OSP +2, possibly by a European major.
Bangchak was heard to have concluded the terms of its crude tender purchase, taking 800,000 barrels of August Murban from a European major at Dubai +76/78, with a 180-day payment period.
Bangchak had earlier requested for a one-year payment period, traders said.
A Korean refiner was also heard buying a VLCC of end July Odudu/Djeno from a European major, but the deal could not be confirmed.--A. Ahmad, Singapore (+65 870 3571)
